context.project: Food delivery platform — back service: NestJS + TypeScript, ESLint (Airbnb preset), Prettier, strict mode. Front service: React + TypeScript + Vitest.

evals.title: Scan fills Naming Conventions from real code
evals.prompt: Scan the back service codebase. Variables use camelCase, classes use PascalCase, files use kebab-case, constants use UPPER_SNAKE, inbound API fields use snake_case, internal code uses camelCase.
expectations: Naming Conventions table has rows for variable, class/type, file, constant, inbound API field
Each row has the correct casing and an example from the repo
Inbound API field row is the casing RULE (snake_case) — not actual field names or shapes
No rows are invented for kinds not observed in the code

evals.title: Scan fills Formatting from formatter config
evals.prompt: The repo has a .prettierrc with: printWidth 100, tabWidth 2, singleQuote true, trailingComma 'all', semi true. Fill the Formatting section.
expectations: other: single quotes, semicolons, trailing comma all
Values come from the config file — not assumed from defaults

evals.title: Programming Practices captured from recurring patterns
evals.prompt: Scanning the back service: every service method wraps calls in try/catch and rethrows as AppException with the original error. Every repository method logs '<ClassName>.<methodName>: <message>' on failure. Every controller validates input with class-validator decorators before processing.
expectations: 3 practice blocks: error handling, logging, validation (or similar names)
Error handling: rule says wrap in try/catch + rethrow as AppException, applies to service methods
Logging: rule says log format '<ClassName>.<methodName>: <message>', applies to repository methods
Validation: rule says use class-validator decorators, applies to controllers
Each block has rule, why, applies to

evals.title: Hard Rules come from user, not from scanning
evals.prompt: Scan the codebase for hard rules.
expectations: Does NOT invent hard rules from scanning the code — hard rules are not scannable
Asks the user for must/never rules
Hard Rules section is empty or TBD until the user provides input
Programming Practices (scannable patterns) are filled separately — they are not hard rules
